$schema: Same shape as benchmarks/judge/cases.json — {criteria, cases[]}. The DIFFERENCE: the fixture is NOT a full security review report. It is the side-by-side EVAL DOCUMENT that the inline LLMJudge gate sees inside the format_report graph node: '## Findings (ground truth)' + '## Proposed TL;DR (under review)'. The criteria below are formatter-specific (do not invent files / CVEs / severities) and grade the TL;DR against the findings section verbatim. Runner: benchmarks.run.run_judge_benchmark with --suite=judge-formatter.

criteria.name: tldr_only_real_files
criteria.description: The 'Proposed TL;DR' section ONLY references file paths that appear in the 'Findings (ground truth)' section above. If the TL;DR mentions a path not listed there, mark as not met.

criteria.name: tldr_only_real_cves
criteria.description: Any CVE id mentioned in the 'Proposed TL;DR' must also appear verbatim in the 'Findings (ground truth)' section. Inventing CVE numbers (or using placeholder shapes like 'CVE-XXXX-XXXX') is not acceptable.

criteria.name: tldr_respects_severity
criteria.description: The TL;DR must not upgrade or downgrade severity buckets. If a finding is listed as `[major]` in the ground truth, the TL;DR may not call it critical (or minor). Severity drift between the ground truth and the TL;DR is a failure.

criteria.name: tldr_no_invented_findings
criteria.description: The TL;DR must not add findings that are absent from the ground truth — no extrapolation ('if this is exploitable then…') and no items the reviewer never produced.
